subject: Demo recap + proposed POC plan — Enterprise Bank
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@enterprisebank.com>, Priya Shah <pshah@enterprisebank.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 12 Mar 2027 13:15:00 -0400
Subject: Demo recap + proposed POC plan — Enterprise Bank

Hi Tom & Priya,

Thanks again for taking the time to join the demo this morning — appreciate the thoughtful questions. Quick recap and next steps so we have everything documented as we discussed: 

TL;DR: Redwood can run a focused POC to validate latency/cost vs. your current setup, verify integration with your redaction pipeline, and measure retrieval/response accuracy on sample queries. Proposed length: 4 weeks.

Key success criteria (what we'd measure during the POC):
- Latency: 95th percentile generation latency under 700ms for typical short queries (~150 tokens).
- Cost: Per-1000-token unit cost reduced by >= 25% vs current baseline (we'll use your sample traffic for benchmarking).
- Functional: >= 90% top-1 relevance on the 150-record evaluation prompt set you shared.
- Security/compliance: Verify audit logs and KMS integration for keys-in-use (no customer data persists on shared hosts).

Proposed evaluation plan (attached as POC-Eval-Plan-EnterpriseBank.xlsx):
1) Week 0 (Prep): Access provisioning, sample data & traffic capture, success criteria sign-off.
2) Week 1 (Integration): Deploy private connector to your test VPC / set up request routing to a sandbox instance; run smoke tests.
3) Week 2 (Baseline & Calibration): Run baseline on your current environment and Redwood hosted variant; collect latency/cost metrics.
4) Week 3 (Iterate & Optimize): Apply batching/quantization and routing policies; re-run benchmarks.
5) Week 4 (Evaluation & Report): Deliver final report, dashboard access, and recommendations.

Ownership and contacts:
- Marissa Cole (Redwood) — overall POC lead and success criteria owner.
- Dev Patel (Redwood) — technical lead for integration, deployment, and logs.
- Rishi Malhotra (Redwood) — performance tuning and benchmarking.
- Priya Shah (Enterprise Bank) — product owner.

Next steps we discussed:
- You to confirm success criteria and approved POC timeline (reply ok to proceed).
- We to provide sandbox access instructions and a DocuSign SOW (if needed for access).
- Schedule a 30-min kickoff — proposed Monday 3/15 10:00am ET (please confirm).

Attachments: POC-Eval-Plan-EnterpriseBank.xlsx (detailed week-by-week plan), SOC2-FAQs-Redwood.pdf (for your security/compliance team).

If any of the success criteria above need to change, flag them and we’ll update the plan before kickoff. Looking forward to getting started.

Best,

Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Thanks Marissa — great recap and thanks for the clear plan. A few questions from our side before we lock dates: 

1) For the latency metric: when you say 95th under 700ms, is that measured from our client to your hosted endpoint or from your internal model runtime only? We need to ensure we can compare apples-to-apples with our current on-prem numbers.

2) Regarding data handling: can you confirm no customer data will be stored on shared hosts and what the retention window is for logs? Our security team will want specific answers so we can sign off quickly.

3) Timing: Monday 3/15 at 10am ET works for a kickoff. Can you have the onboarding checklist and sandbox instructions ready by Monday morning?

Also — what level of support is included during the POC (office hours vs. dedicated engineer)?

Thanks,
Tom
Director, AI Platforms
Enterprise Bank
+1 (212) 555-0123

Hi Tom — quick answers inline below and some clarifications: 

1) Latency measurement: we’ll measure end-to-end from a synthetic client in your test VPC to the Redwood runtime (so it includes network hops). For an apples-to-apples baseline, we’ll run the same synthetic client against your on-prem endpoint and compare the two. We’ll include p50/p95/p99 in the dashboard.

2) Data handling & logs: we do not persist customer request payloads on shared hosts. Audit logs (metadata only) are retained for 90 days by default in the sandbox; for Dedicated or Private deployments we can adjust retention per contract. KMS integration is supported — keys remain in your KMS and are not exported. Please see the attached SOC2-FAQs-Redwood.pdf for standard answers; happy to get your security team on a call if they need more detail.

3) Support level: POC includes up to 5 hours/week of dedicated engineering time for integration and tuning. If you need on-call coverage during a specific milestone we can provide it as an add-on.

Kickoff: we’ll send a calendar invite for Mon 15 Mar 2027 10:00am ET and include an onboarding checklist.

Action items for Monday:
- Priya/Tom: Confirm the evaluation prompt set (Priya said she would share the 150 prompts).
- Enterprise Bank: Provide test VPC access details and the contact to provision the service account.
- Redwood: Share sandbox access docs and SOW/DocuSign link.

Looping in Dev and Rishi to own the sandbox deployment and load test plan.

Thanks — Marissa

Hi all — quick technical notes ahead of Monday’s kickoff: 

- Access: Please send the VPC peering details or the test VPC CIDR and the principal to add for the service account. We’ll provide explicit IPs and a short checklist for firewall rules.
- Sandbox timeline: I’ll have a basic sandbox instance up within 24 hours of receiving access; full load testing hooks and dashboards should be ready within 48–72 hours after that.
- Metrics we’ll publish: p50/p95/p99 latency, tokens per second, cost-per-1k-tokens (estimated), and top-1/top-3 relevance on the evaluation set.
- Logs/retention: for the sandbox we’ll enable audit logs for 90 days and provide an export if you want to ingest them into your SIEM.

If you prefer, we can do a 20-min technical sync right after the kickoff to walk through access and the smoke test checklist.

Thanks — looking forward to it.
